main_text.p: curæ habebant, ut frumentum, farina, panes æquo pretio venderentur, in urbe assiduò degentes x, in Piræo v, & litigantibus ibi jus dicentes; instítutum utilissimum & æquissimum: ut & alterum de ἀγορανόμοις & μετρονόμοις.

Quorum priores ἀγορανόμοι x numero, forte lecti, curabant forum reliquarum rerum venalium excepto frumento, quini in urbe, quini in Piræo, dabantque præcipuè operam, ne quid fieret immodestè, neve mendaciis se mutuò circumvenirent ementes & vendentes. Μετρονόμοι menfurarum, ut justæ essent, quibus vendentes utebantur, nescio an & ponderum rationem habebant, quinque in Piræo, quod emporium urbis erat, decem in urbe. Collimabant etiam ad eandem boni publici curam qui dicebantur ἐπιμελητὴς[?] ἐμπορίου, quibus lex præcipiebat hoc ut agerent, ne importati frumenti copia civitas Attica destitueretur, & avaritia civium alió frumentum devectantium reipublicæ fraudi esset. Erant & ναυ-κληρικῷ[?] navicularis & mercatoribus inter se lites habentibus operam dantes, deque peregrinatione etiam jus dicentes, & ἐπωγωγεῖς[?] & similes alii. Et præ-

page.notes: Greek words are copied from a small, low-resolution scan; accents and breathings are uncertain, so the Greek is marked [?] where the letters are doubtful: ἐπιμελητὴς, ναυκληρικῷ, ἐπωγωγεῖς. The Greek ἀγορανόμοι and μετρονόμοι are printed with a rough breathing; the breathing marks are not fully clear. "alió" is read with an accent that may be an acute. The running head is printed "ATHENIENSIVM"; per the u/v rule it is given as "ATHENIENSIUM". Page ends mid-word at "præ-", continued on the next page. The faint marks at the left edge and the bottom-right fragment are show-through or the neighbouring page and are not transcribed.
